item.title: Wow
item.content:encoded: I read this story back in I think 2018, and I can't believe I never wrote a comment on it until now. Or I did, and I forgot. This story is incredible, and it's stories like this that are why I can't get enough of the SCP Universe. Even more so hearing that it isn't canon, because you still managed to make it something as professional as a canon back story. I absolutely love the way you write "it takes the wound a moment to bleed" then copy the events as they repeat after TJ takes the pain. The way you write about the guns jamming for the first and last time. Going around something with hinting descriptions rather than outright saying something. A lot is said through this story, and yet a lot is untold, left to the reader to decide what follows at certain points. Honestly, you get those scenes where someone get's cozy with a blanket, sitting in a recliner next to a fire, putting on their glasses and reading a good book to pass the time. This is a story I'd read like that. I get chills, I feel sad, and my heart even races when I read this. I could keep rambling on and on but to wrap this up I'll say; Well done. This is nothing short of a masterpiece in my eyes, and it says even more that you impressed Bright himself. Hat's off to you.

item.title: Bright Family Reference
item.content:encoded:
Hey, I'm kinda realizing here that some people have not been also intensely reading Bright family canon for 8 months now, so I'm just gonna kinda insert the family reference chart we built in the SCP Shitposting discord here:

+ Show hell map
- Hide hell map

This also isn't a full reference, either. Like, duckman likes to change his canon, which is cool but like. Help

+ Show brightcanon.jpg
- Hide brightcanon.jpg

And yeah, a few minor discrepancies in this tale:
1. As Duckman said, I didn't mention Sarah. I actually thought about inserting a chapter with Mikell and Jack reminiscing on their experience of their mom's stillbirth (burying the empty box and stuff, but their parents never mention it again and they aren't aware of their sibling until they enter the Foundation) but I was afraid it would pull from the focus of the piece.

2. Mikell has two children; in Duckman's canon he only has one. Take this as you will.
EDIT: after looking at the map, this is already true. Good for me.

3. Canonically, Claire can see the future, but not change the timeline to suit her needs as she does during Mikell's rodeo in this tale. That being said, she's referenced as a very powerful seer in other tales.

4. Other Bright family reading from Duckman's canon:
-"I Quit"
-Here There Be (I ignore this one, mostly because it hasn't happened yet for the majority of the tale, or maybe doesn't happen at all)
-RIP
-Code Brown
-What Is Love?
-Nothing to See Here (Linked and referenced in Mikell's sidepage in this tale)
-Blind Date
-And then of course, like, 45 other ones that relate in one way or another, but the main canon one regarding family dynamics- and the one I was kind of enchanted/entranced by, and still am- Is Code Brown.

5. One of the things I played a lot with in this tale was the idea that all of the Bright kids were born anomolous in one way or another, like a genetic trait. Mikell's- and this isn't quite obvious, but I'm rolling with it- is his connection to the guns, which are heavily anomalous and in some ways sapient artifacts that don't really accept owners unconditionally, at least in this tale.

6. I was worried about this tale because it doesn't really match with these other Bright tales in a lot of ways, but mostly in tone/subject matter. Duckman's tales are enchanting, wild, lighthearted but complex tales that have quite a bit of humor. They don't take themselves seriously. This one is meant to be dark, rich, emotional, and striking. For a while, I had this named Midwestern Gothic, and I would still put it in the Gothic genre to some degree; it's connected to nature, to environments, to emotions and similar feelings of numbness and anger felt by someone in Jack's position as he learns how to work with his mental health as he enters his adult life, and how his position as a Director/contained artifact affects that. It's unusually serious subject manner.

item.title: Whooo.
item.content:encoded:
Well. This is… this is something else really.

This is quite frankly amazing. There are hints, and references to Bright canon in here that just make my day and squee… Stuff like gambling, or him making moonshine.

And you're right, it's not canon. The Bright family were city dwellers. There's no mention of Sarah. Their family, or their father at least, wouldn't have left them alone like that.

But, that being said, I'm not critting it for canon. This is… freaking amazing. I mean, uneblievably huge, and awesome, and… There are things here that fit in despite me not ever putting them out, mostly in the relationships between peoples.

(Also, I've been trying to write an SCP about Space Oddity for YEARS.)

Honestly… yes, it's not-canon. But, in my head, it's not-canon in the same way as Unfinished Business. It's not what I would have done with the characters. It's not nessacarily using all of my head canon. But whereas some stories are simply Not. Canon. This is OFFICIALLY Not-Canon. Like, I'm proud to have created the characters that were used in this.

I really like how bits feel pulled from my brain, like how the first bit doesn't use any names, something I often avoid in my writings. I like how you took it and made it your own, even after hearing from me what I considered canon. Honestly, in my head, it does kind of make me wanna change Bright to depressive before the amulet. It makes sense.

Not only that, but you stumbled on a power I didn't know he had… The universe refuses to let Bright die. Something always happens… until it found an easy way to keep him safe.

Hmmm.

Wishing I could vote multiple times, all of them Plus.

(also congrats on getting the longest response from me in… I think ever.)

item.content:encoded:
A few months back, me and Roget were discussing ideas by which we could increase the visibility of tales. We discussed this and we both concluded that we'd really like to see a tale project with scale: something large and frightening in scope that rocks canon to its core, that tears your envisioning of the Foundation from tip to toe as you realise just what you've read.

Whether it's Incident 239-B's large-scale havoc involving giants of the site canon throwing down against one another with an innocent girl's life in the balance, Duke 'til Dawn's pinnacle of self-insert insanity or the slow, creeping, painful dissection of a major character's psyche in In His Own Image, when they're done right tales can split the readerbase in twain and shape the future of site canons for years to come.

Is it too early to say whether or not this is one of them?

Probably, but it won't stop me applauding you on writing one of the most ambitious, well-written and deeply immersive pieces of fiction on this site.

I hope to see someone cite this as a reason why they came to the site in the same way hundreds of newbies have been pulled in by the decommissionings, the Duchamps and the Game Days. Well done.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Though I'm past one hundred thousand miles
I'm feeling very still
And I think my spaceship knows which way to go…
…Planet Earth is blue
And there's nothing I can do.

This took me

8 MONTHS TO WRITE

It's easily the longest fiction work I've writen so far in my entire life. A few brief notes about this wild time:
1. This wasn't the kind of tale you choose to write. I don't know how this happened. This started as a fanfic, and then became serious very quickly.

2. I asked theduckman, about a third of the way into this project, if Jack had depression before the amulet in his canon. He said no. I then decided to just kinda casually throw out his entire canon to make my own to make this work, because there is no canon and all associated remarks. So to keep things straight, I have to note here: this does not take place inside theduckman's canon. It takes place, technically, in a separate hell canon where no one is happy and bad things happen to everyone.

3. I struggled for a long time over what to name this, before settling on the famous David Bowie character who becomes lost in space after takeoff and subsequently is never heard from again.

4. Special thanks to Cyan for letting me use their heke rad texting/pager code block format for the texts between Bright and Gears (it's from their super rad and cool tale "Coming Down" and you should read it its good)

5. This was written after me having the worst mental health year of my life last year, and is partially drawn off of that experience

6. All pictures in the weird side-tale thingys are taken by me for the purpose of this tale, and I wrote the code for those myself. I guess you could call me a hacker or something

7. I no longer know what to do with my life now that this is over what do I even do??? we just dont know

A brief weird kind of reflection: 2/13/2019
I just listened to Space Oddity again for the first time in a long time, and I had a second to reflect. It's been a couple years- I wrote this in high school, and I'm almost halfway through college now- but it's absolutely incredible to me how tied I feel to this story. As soon as the opening bars of that song play, I feel almost homesick. I remember everything about this like it's a physical place I can visit; from what I was feeling when I wrote it to what I imagined Jack's surroundings to look like.

It's almost at 100+ now. Unlike some of the other stories I've written I feel like this one really stands the test of time, and as of now I continue to stand by it. There are a few changes I would make if I were to write it now, I think, but for the most part…I still adore this one. I'm glad it's continuing to be special to other people the way it's special to me. I don't think I'll ever be able to forget this story and the unique kind of bleak, melancholy warmth it has, and the weird comfort it brings revisiting it.
